parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or sea
to lam is to thrash or hit

explanation.surface: Things kick off noisily once someone's backside is smacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, after the old London asylum, is a name for chaotic noise and confusion, a synonym for uproar.

parts.note: to bet is to venture a stake

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Someone takes up half a risky venture at the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns SEMI into IMES beneath BET in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Betimes is an old adverb for in good time or early in the morning.

clue.text: Live, having died in good health

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died in records
to be well is to be in good health

explanation.surface: A paradox: someone lived on despite dying in perfect health.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there, a verb synonym for residing.

clue.text: Giant elm to be replaced around noon, or evening

indicators.note: around says the reshuffled letters wrap about the abbreviation for noon
the letters of the giant elm are replaced in a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A huge elm tree is due to be swapped out at midday or later in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced' shuffles GIANTELM into ALIGMENT, and 'around' wraps it round N. 'evening' wants to be a time of day after noon; it is the noun from making even.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening things up, making them level or straight, is bringing them into alignment.

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
a rent is a tear or cut

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob may be appearing in the musical Rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is itself a musical, which tempts the solver to treat it as one piece; it is the cut, and Hair is the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one style of trimmed hair, so it is an example of the wider class.

clue.text: Someone held socks with name inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for a name sits within the word for socks

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: Someone holds a pair of socks with a name written inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security, so someone held fits.

indicators.note: away says the abbreviation for right is taken out of the first name

parts.note: Indira Gandhi was prime minister of ...

explanation.surface: A nation needs Gandhi's leadership immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'at once', but 'right' gives R and 'away' removes it from INDIRA. The famous Gandhi, Mahatma, is the false trail; it is Indira.
explanation.definitionFit: India is the South Asian republic, a country as the clue asks.

clue.text: Mixture of feta and rice served by a restaurant

indicators.note: served by means placed next to, so the article follows the mixed letters
a mixture blends things together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A dish of feta and rice brought out by a waiter in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture of' shuffles FETARICE into CAFETERI, and 'served by' puts A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, a particular kind of eatery.

parts.note: read as a farmyard bird that has no cause to celebrate the festive season, since it ends up on the table; it is also a nation

explanation.surface: A nation where the festive season is not marked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a non-Christian nation; the joke is that the traditional festive roast bird is hardly celebrating either.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is both the country straddling Europe and Asia and the bird roasted for Christmas dinner.

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: Someone's resolve weakens as they hit the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider.

annotationWithheld.why: Put off effin' Bambi! (5): DEFER is F inside DEER, where 'effin'' gives F and is also the 'in' insertion signal, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Article in use fraudulently hidden by a novelist

indicators.note: in places the article within the word for exploiting

parts.note: to milk a scheme is to exploit or use it dishonestly
an is the indefinite article
something hidden by a thing lies under it

explanation.surface: An item in a fraud case is concealed by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article in use' tempts an anagram of IN USE, but 'fraudulently' belongs with 'use', and 'hidden by a' reads as UNDER A, what lies beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan Kundera was the Czech-born writer of The Unbearable Lightness of Being, a novelist.

clue.text: Argue about holding stake in contract

indicators.note: holding says the reshuffled letters contain the word for a stake
about signals the letters of argue are turned around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
the ante is the stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: Two parties dispute a contract clause involving a held stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ARGUE into GUARE; an ante is the opening poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal promise or agreement, a binding contract of assurance.

clue.text: Rush over to see naval doctor

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush
on can mean over, as in a tax on or over goods

explanation.surface: A sailor hurries across to consult the ship's medic.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval medical officers carry the rank title surgeon, as in Surgeon Commander.

clue.text: Supermarket trolleys with locked brakes aren't creased up

definitions.text: Supermarket trolleys with locked brakes aren't
definitions.meaning: literally, trolleys whose brakes are locked are not moving freely along the shop's walkways
creased up means helpless with laughter

explanation.surface: Shopping carts with jammed brakes are not doubled over with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes freely moving trolleys between the shelves, and idiomatically means laughing uncontrollably, as an audience does in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an audience helpless with laughter is a picture of people literally rolling about the walkways.

indicators.note: withdraws means the setter's word steps backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
read as BER twice over, the word is a plural: two lots of BER, so BERS

explanation.surface: The compiler retreats, while a North African tribesman stays behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdraws' turns ME into EM. The North African people are a red herring: Paul's joke reads the word as a pair of BERs.
explanation.definitionFit: Embers are the glowing remains of a fire, what is left after burning.

clue.text: Journalist given second parting drink finds little room

indicators.note: parting means splitting the drink so the other pieces go into the gap

parts.note: bitter is a British style of draught beer
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter with a second farewell drink ends up in a tiny flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale; a bedsitter is the British word for a bedsit, one room to sleep and live in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsitter is a British one-room flat serving as bedroom and sitting room, a little room to live in.

parts.note: flat means level or smooth
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A calm, steady breeze blowing from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as weather; it is gas in the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatus is the medical term for intestinal gas, or wind in the stomach.

parts.note: the shin is the shinbone, the tibia
to dig something is slang for liking or enjoying it

explanation.surface: A bone gets to enjoy a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is a British term for a boisterous party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a noisy party, as is a knees-up, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Lad scrabbled through impenetrable stuff, as scavenger

indicators.note: through says the scrambled letters run inside the word for murky stuff

parts.note: murk is thick darkness or gloom that cannot be seen through

indicators.note: scrabbled suggests scrambling about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A boy scrabbles through thick sludge, hunting for scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrabbled' jumbles LAD into DLA. Mudlarks combed the Thames mud at low tide for saleable finds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudlark scavenged the Thames mud for saleable objects, so a scavenger.

parts.note: to mug is to attack and rob
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, president of the United States

explanation.surface: A call to assault a particular head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe Lincoln gives the letters; the whole clue suggests the Zimbabwean leader himself as a president one might wish to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Mugabe was the long-ruling president of Zimbabwe, the one the clue invites the solver to target.

clue.text: Word of enlightenment locks agricultural labourer up again

indicators.note: locks means holds fast, so the exclamation encloses the other piece

parts.note: ah is what someone says when they suddenly understand

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a serf was a feudal farm labourer

explanation.surface: A cry of understanding comes as a farmworker is locked up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SERF into FRES in this down entry; the exclamation is the sound of the penny dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew or again, starting over.

clue.text: Evidence of supernatural beings managing to pass round single track

indicators.note: to pass round says the word for managing goes around the other pieces

parts.note: faring means managing or getting on
I, the Roman numeral for one, is single
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Proof of fairies appears when someone circles a lone railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single track' reads as one rail line, I plus RY; folklore says rings of toadstools mark where fairies danced.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy ring is a circle of mushrooms in grass, said in folklore to mark where fairies danced.

definitions.meaning: the quantity of crop gathered from a field
a command to surrender or concede

explanation.definitionFit: Yield is both the amount a crop produces and a verb meaning to surrender.

parts.note: Io is one of the moons of Jupiter
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Is a ghostly white politician a lunar figure?
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' looks like a politician; read as state's man it means a man of a US state, here Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a native of the US state of Iowa, so a man from a state.

parts.note: W, west, is a compass bearing
an inch is a short measure of length

explanation.surface: A lift moves something a very short way.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a hoisting device, and to winch is to lift or haul something.

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: a beagle is a hound used for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A bird of prey's hunter has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunter' wants to describe the bird; it is the beagle hound, losing its B.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Hollow thing turning into poet for woman entering high society

indicators.note: into says the turned piece goes inside the poet's name

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: turning says the hollow object is read backwards

parts.note: a tube is a hollow cylinder

explanation.surface: A hollow cylinder twists into a poet's work about a young society woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TUBE into EBUT; 'Hollow thing' is any tube, not the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her formal entrance into fashionable society.

parts.note: to hang is to execute on the gallows
a dog is a contemptible or wicked fellow

explanation.surface: A villain is put to death, as befits the guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced or guilty, so the adjectives are synonyms.

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the composer's name is dropped

parts.note: Johannes Brahms was the German Romantic composer

explanation.surface: A composer is something less than a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts the S from BRAHMS, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahma is the Hindu creator deity, one of the principal gods of the Trimurti.
